memo.thesis_en: I own this stock, and I am keeping it. The measurable evidence matches what I look for: revenue compounding at 18.5% a year over five years, R&D at 28.5% of revenue, a 41.4% operating margin that has widened by about 343 basis points over five years, and a share count down 10.9%. A P/E of 26.8 is not an extravagant price for that kind of business. Being down 9.2% in 42 days is price noise, and price is not one of my three reasons to sell. But I must be honest about the gaps. I have no scuttlebutt in front of me, no verified view of management integrity, and no way to check the ten qualitative points, so I would not add until that work is done. As I wrote, 'the time to sell it is — almost never' if the job was done correctly, and I intend to finish that job.

memo.thesis_en: I own this business, and I keep it. The measurable evidence is what I look for in a compounder: five-year revenue growth of 14.57% a year, an operating margin of 46.78% that has widened by about 519 basis points over five years, and a share count down 1.22%. Debt to equity is 0.075, so growth is not being financed with borrowed money or new shares. Honesty requires me to say what this snapshot cannot tell me. It contains no scuttlebutt, no integrity evidence, and no industry margin, retention or turnover figures. I therefore hold with modest confidence and verify the qualitative points rather than assume them, and I will not add until they are checked. A 2.46% paper loss after four days is noise, and as I wrote, the time to sell a correctly chosen stock is almost never.

memo.thesis_en: I own this company, 11 shares bought at $48.33 and now showing a 37.34% gain. I will not sell because the price has risen; as I wrote in Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits, a gain is not a reason to sell. What the numbers show is encouraging: R&D at 26.72% of revenue, margins up about 411 basis points over five years, and a share count that has barely moved. At 27 times earnings with trailing revenue growth near 10%, the price is full, so I would not add. The questions that matter most, management integrity and candor, are not answered by this snapshot, and I cannot call the integrity check passed without that scuttlebutt. I hold under the Motorola discipline until a real thesis-breaking trigger appears, and I will do the missing work before ever adding.
memo.thesis_he: אני מחזיק במניה הזו: 11 מניות שנקנו ב-48.33 דולר, ובמחיר הנוכחי הרווח עומד על 37.34%. אני לא מוכר רק כי המחיר עלה; כפי שכתבתי ב'מניות רגילות ורווחים בלתי רגילים', רווח אינו סיבה למכור. המספרים מעודדים: מחקר ופיתוח בשיעור 26.72% מההכנסות, שולי רווח שעלו בכ-411 נקודות בסיס בחמש שנים, ומספר מניות שכמעט לא זז. אבל במכפיל של 27 ועם צמיחת הכנסות היסטורית של כ-10%, המחיר מלא, ולכן אין סיבה להוסיף. השאלות החשובות מכולן, יושרה וגילוי לב של ההנהלה, אינן נענות בנתונים שלפניי, ואני לא יכול לקבוע שבדיקת היושרה עברה בלי מחקר 'סקאטלבאט' שעוד לא נעשה. אני מחזיק בדיסציפלינה של מוטורולה עד שיופיע טריגר אמיתי שסותר את התזה, ולפני כל הוספה אשלים את העבודה החסרה.
